extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Spectator / general early-18th-century literate public; aspiring periodical essayists and moralists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative remarks aimed at authors of periodical essays and general writers, covering habits of composition, moral qualifications for criticism, the purpose of print, use of imagination/dreams for practice, and the desired durability/finish of works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Itch of Writing (Cacoethes) / epidemic of scribbling
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a certain Distemper ... the Itch of Writing. This Cacoethes is as Epidemical as the Small-Pox, there being very few who are not seized with it some time or other in their Lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge that a compulsive tendency to write is common and often incurable; be self-aware about compulsive publication. The passage criticises overproduction and frames habitual scribbling as a malady requiring restraint (e.g., 'forbidding him the use of Pen, Ink and Paper' as a cure in extreme cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism of Periodical Writers / avoid perpetual, never-ending publication
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no Species of Scriblers more offensive, and more incurable, than your Periodical Writers, whose Works return upon the Publick on certain Days and at stated Times. We have not the Consolation ... that we are sure if we have but Patience, we may come to the End of their Labours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not produce periodic pieces merely to refill a schedule; avoid creating a sense of endless drudgery for readers. Ensure individual pieces have shape, value and (where appropriate) a satisfying end rather than endless continuation for its own sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Printing: convey truth and knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a melancholy thing to consider, that the Art of Printing, which might be the greatest Blessing to Mankind, should prove detrimental to us, and that it should be made use of to scatter Prejudice and Ignorance through a People, instead of conveying to them Truth and Knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the press responsibly: favour truth, education and genuine enlightenment over the spread of prejudice, ignorance or mere noise. Publishing should aim to improve public understanding rather than inflame or mislead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors as luminous or tenebrificous stars (enlighten, don't darken)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some [authors] are Stars that scatter Light as others do Darkness. I could mention several Authors who are tenebrificous Stars of the first Magnitude ... The Nation has been a great while benighted with several of these Antiluminaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aspire to be an 'illuminating' writer; avoid producing work that confuses, misleads or 'darkens' public discourse. The metaphor counsels writers to add light rather than perpetuate obscurity or dullness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of imagination/dreams as rehearsal and self-discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Night before they slept they should examine what they had been a doing that Day ... in a Morning before my Scholar rose, he should consider what he had been about that Night ... To go to Bed with a Mind entirely free from Passion, and a Body clear of the least Intemperance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt concrete practices to harness imagination: nightly review of the day's actions and intentions, morning reflection on nocturnal imaginings, and prepare body/mind (avoid intemperance and passion before sleep) so that dreams can productively rehearse, clarify and practice waking tasks and creative projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearse important tasks in imagination (sleep as preparatory workshop)
rubrics_metrics.description: If I have any Business of consequence to do to-morrow, I am scarce dropt asleep to-night but I am in the midst of it, and when awake I consider the whole Procession of the Affair, and get the Advantage of the next Day's Experience before the Sun has risen upon it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentally run through an important piece of writing or action before sleep as a method of planning and problem-solving; imagination can provide anticipatory practice that improves waking performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral qualification for criticism: purify self before censuring others
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you can be qualified to see and animadvert on the Failings of others, you must be pure your self.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics and essayists should practice self-examination and attend to their own faults before publicly censuring others; moral humility and self-purification are prerequisites for legitimate critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance publication frequency and length/compensate scarcity with substance
rubrics_metrics.description: What's the Reason that while you only talk now upon Wednesdays, Fridays, and Mondays, you pretend to be a greater Tatler, than when you spoke every Day as you formerly used to do? If this be your plunging out of your Taciturnity, pray let the Length of your Speeches compensate for the Scarceness of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If publishing less frequently, ensure each piece carries proportionate weight and substance; scarcity of output can be justified by greater length or depth, but avoid thin long pieces that merely pad infrequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid prolixity (excessive wordiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Philanthropos is, I dare say, a very well-meaning Man, but a little too prolix in his Compositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep prose disciplined and avoid unnecessary verbosity; concision improves clarity and reader enjoyment. Prolixity is explicitly flagged as a fault even in well-meaning writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate durable, improving works (planting as model for creative labour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plantations have one Advantage in them ... they give a Pleasure of a more lasting Date, and continually improve in the Eye of the Planter ... when you have finished your Plantations, they are still arriving at greater Degrees of Perfection as long as you live.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor projects that mature and improve over time; conceive writing and other creative labours like planting—efforts that yield increasing satisfaction and public benefit across years rather than ephemeral glory.
